blocker_history.was: On vcptcore-qa1 the file-upload scope 'product-configuration' was not registered in FileExperienceApi. Every upload returned HTTP 200 with succeeded:false / INVALID_SCOPE, so no file could be attached and the ticket was unreachable. The storefront rendered an optimistic '100% done' over the failed request, which read as a validation defect and stalled two browser agents on two different lanes.
blocker_history.hypothesis_FALSIFIED: The pre-fix hypothesis was 'VirtoCommerce.Catalog 3.1042.0 -> 3.1044.0'. It is WRONG. After the fix Catalog is STILL 3.1042.0, and a before/after diff of GET /api/platform/modules shows ZERO module-level change: 92 installed both times, no version moved, none added, none removed. Scope registration therefore does NOT track a module version on this platform — it is configuration- or startup-dependent, so it can regress silently on any environment with every version table looking correct. Probe the endpoint, never infer from versions.
blocker_history.collateral_while_broken: Also blocked the 9 pre-existing CFG-FILE-* cases in regression/suites/Frontend/configurable-products/072b-file-text-section-cases.csv on this environment.

deployed.probe: GET /api/platform/modules, authenticated — ground truth, not the declared manifest

mechanism_established_live.upload: POST /api/files/product-configuration (FileExperienceApi scope, multipart) -> [{succeeded, scope, name, size, contentType, id, url, publicUrl}]. url is RELATIVE: /api/files/<id>.
mechanism_established_live.attach: addItem(command: InputAddItemType) carries configurationSections: [ConfigurationSectionInput{sectionId, type, option, customText, fileUrls}]. fileUrls is a CLIENT-supplied list of strings — the server does not mint the URL inside the configuration mutation.
mechanism_established_live.read: files{url,name,size,contentType} on CartConfigurationItemType, OrderConfigurationItemType AND QuoteConfigurationItemType. The ticket names only cart/checkout/order; quote is an unstated fourth surface.
mechanism_established_live.extension_allowlist: .doc .rtf .docx .txt .pdf .xls .xlsx .jpg .png .odt — enforced by EXTENSION, not content: the same bytes renamed .txt pass where .csv is rejected with INVALID_EXTENSION. Note .html is NOT allowed, which removes much of the 'open an attacker's page in a new tab' risk.
mechanism_established_live.disposition: The file endpoint always returns content-disposition: attachment, even for image/png. Activating the URL DOWNLOADS; it never opens inline.
mechanism_established_live.access_control: Layered, and it changes at order placement. UNATTACHED freshly-uploaded file: readable by anyone (allowAnonymousUpload is declared for this scope). ATTACHED TO A CART: anonymous 403, a different buyer 403, the OWNER 200 — correct. ATTACHED TO AN ORDER: the OWNER also gets 403, which is defect F3. An admin token reads it 200 throughout, so the file is intact and servable at every stage.
mechanism_established_live.storefront_proxy_auth: The storefront domain is cookie-session based and returns 401 for a bearer token, which is why the link must be verified in a browser rather than by curl.
mechanism_established_live.constraints_source_of_truth: GraphQL query fileUploadOptions(scope: String) -> FileUploadScopeOptionsType{scope, maxFileSize, allowedExtensions, allowAnonymousUpload}. For product-configuration: maxFileSize 10000000, the 10-extension allowlist, and allowAnonymousUpload declared — so anonymous upload to this scope is configured behaviour, not an oversight. The storefront dropzone copy renders from this query.

findings_pending_triage.claim: The PDP File dropzone tells the customer 'The files available for upload are in any formats', which is false. The server enforces an extension allowlist and rejects anything outside it with INVALID_EXTENSION.
findings_pending_triage.evidence: POST /api/files/product-configuration with vcst5924-bravo.csv -> succeeded:false, errorCode INVALID_EXTENSION, errorMessage 'Allowed file extensions: .doc, .rtf, .docx, .txt, .pdf, .xls, .xlsx, .jpg, .png, .odt'. The identical bytes renamed .txt -> succeeded:true.
findings_pending_triage.provenance: PRE-EXISTING — the copy predates this ticket and belongs to the upload surface, not to the preview feature
findings_pending_triage.note: Matches the domain map's D2/G2: the constraint copy traced to neither Admin nor the schema. The allowlist is now that missing source of truth.
findings_pending_triage.retraction_reason: The 'any formats / 1MB' dropzone copy was an ARTIFACT OF THE BROKEN ENVIRONMENT, not a product defect. The copy is data-driven from the GraphQL query fileUploadOptions(scope:'product-configuration'), which returns maxFileSize 10000000 (rendered as 9.5 MB) and allowedExtensions exactly matching the server allowlist. While the scope was unregistered that query returned nothing and the UI fell back to a generic string, which is what the two pre-fix agents saw. Re-observed live post-fix, the dropzone states the exact allowlist and 9.5 MB. Do not file.
findings_pending_triage.useful_residue: Two things worth keeping. (1) The source of truth for the file constraints is fileUploadOptions — this closes the domain map's G2/G6, which recorded the 1MB/5-file numbers as untraceable. (2) A dropzone reading 'any formats' is now a usable DIAGNOSTIC that the scope is unregistered, since the real copy always names the allowlist.

findings_pending_triage.claim: The ticket asks for a URL 'so I can either open or download the file', but the endpoint always sends content-disposition: attachment — including for image/png. Nothing can ever open inline.
findings_pending_triage.evidence: curl -D - on /api/files/<id> as the owner -> 'content-disposition: attachment; filename=vcst5924-alpha.txt'

findings_pending_triage.note: Not necessarily a defect. It is the question the author has to answer, now measured rather than speculated.

findings_pending_triage.claim: The file's read grant is scoped to the CART and is not carried over to the ORDER. Once the cart converts, the owner gets 403 on a URL the order's own GraphQL response still advertises.
evidence: Same buyer, same file id: 200 from the cart (pre-order), 403 after placing order CO260916-00001 — reproduced at the API level independently of the browser
Admin token reads the same file: 200, 28 bytes, correct content — the file is intact and servable
A freshly uploaded, unattached file read by the SAME buyer: 200 — the buyer's read path works in general
findings_pending_triage.note: This is the ticket's requirement 3. Two defects stacked: the backend missing order-scoped grant (the blocker), and the frontend hard-navigating to a full-page 403 instead of surfacing an inline error (separable, Medium).

findings_pending_triage.claim: The attachment is not a URL. It renders as a role=button with a JS download handler and no href, so there is no open-in-new-tab, middle-click, copy-link or save-as, on any of the three surfaces.
evidence: a11y tree: button 'vcst5924-charlie.png,' with no /url, while the sibling 'Edit configuration' in the same block IS a real link and does expose its /url
Ctrl+click downloaded in place instead of opening a tab
Combined with the always-attachment disposition (F2), 'open' is impossible for every type including image/png

findings_pending_triage.claim: Order Details drops the Section column that cart and checkout show, and reorders the rows, so a past order does not say which requirement each attachment satisfied.

Separator comma is baked into the control's accessible name: a screen reader announces 'vcst5924-charlie.png,' with the punctuation as part of the filename. The collapsed row also renders a bare trailing comma.

The order details page fetches a vendor logo from raw.githubusercontent.com and it fails with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB. A storefront pulling an asset from GitHub raw is both broken and a supply-chain smell.
Attaching MORE than 5 files to a configuration File section silently destroys data: the mutation returns success with no error and the cart keeps only the LAST file, discarding the rest.
evidence: addItem with 6 fileUrls -> HTTP 200, no errors[], cart stores 1 (c6.txt)
addItem with 7 fileUrls -> HTTP 200, no errors[], cart stores 1 (c7.txt)
Confirmed by re-reading each cart independently of the mutation response
findings_pending_triage.provenance: PRE-EXISTING — this is the attach path, which predates the preview feature this ticket adds
findings_pending_triage.reachability: Low through the storefront UI, which enforces 5 client-side; real for any other API consumer (integration, a different storefront, a mobile app). The server exposes no maxFileCount in fileUploadOptions, so the 5 is a client-only rule.
findings_pending_triage.expected: Either reject the request with an explicit error naming the limit (as the size check already does with INVALID_SIZE), or store the first 5. Silently keeping one is the worst of the three.

findings_pending_triage.claim: The order of attached files is not preserved. Five files submitted as c1..c5 came back as c2,c3,c1,c4,c5, and the desktop UI rendered the two-file case in reverse of the submitted order.

A ZERO-BYTE file is accepted by the server on a required File section, while the existing regression case CFG-FILE-003 asserts it is rejected. The validation is presumably client-side only, so the server has no defence in depth.

findings_pending_triage.claim: A mobile agent reported a P0 "cart read path and write path target two different carts". INVESTIGATED AND RETRACTED — it was MY OWN test residue, not a product defect.
findings_pending_triage.retraction_reason: The cart the storefront rendered was id 58fed74d, which a carts{} query showed to be named 'countprobe7' — one of three NAMED carts I created minutes earlier while testing the file-count limit. Mutations correctly targeted the 'default' cart and persisted everything. The storefront simply picked up one of the extra named carts. A real buyer never creates named carts through the UI, so this is not reachable in the product. The three probe carts have been deleted (removeCart); only 'default' remains.
findings_pending_triage.lesson: Creating named carts on a shared fixture account pollutes what the storefront shows to any later session. Use one cart name, or delete named carts immediately.

findings_pending_triage.claim: .jpeg is rejected by the upload allowlist while .jpg is allowed.
findings_pending_triage.evidence: POST /api/files/product-configuration with photo.jpeg -> INVALID_SIZE? no: INVALID_EXTENSION. The declared allowlist is .doc .rtf .docx .txt .pdf .xls .xlsx .jpg .png .odt.
findings_pending_triage.note: .jpeg is a common photo extension. Allowing .jpg but not .jpeg reads as an oversight in the configured list rather than a deliberate policy.

findings_pending_triage.claim: An oversized upload is accepted in full before the size check runs, and it can be done anonymously.
evidence: 50 MB anonymous -> 52,428,998 bytes sent over 13.8 s, then HTTP 200 with INVALID_SIZE (limit 10,000,000). Same on the storefront proxy and on the backend directly.
100 MB authenticated -> 100,000,199 bytes sent over 22.6 s, then INVALID_SIZE.
1 GB -> HTTP 413 from Cloudflare after 1,343,488 bytes — so the edge, not the application, is what bounds this.
findings_pending_triage.expected: Reject on Content-Length before reading the body, so a request 5x over the limit costs one round trip rather than 50 MB of ingest.
findings_pending_triage.mitigation_note: Bounded above by the Cloudflare body cap, which is why this is Medium and not High.

The order's GraphQL still returns files{url,name,size,contentType}, but GET /api/files/{id} returns 403 to the file's own owner once the cart becomes an order, so the API advertises a URL the owner is forbidden to fetch. Requirements 1 and 2 render and download, but not via a URL, which is what the ticket asked for.

extension_matrix.method: POST /api/files/product-configuration, one probe file per extension
extension_matrix.verdict: PASS — the allowlist is complete and symmetric; every allowed extension is accepted and every probed disallowed one returns INVALID_EXTENSION

content_type_derivation.finding: contentType is derived from the EXTENSION, not from the bytes. Plain-text probes were stored as application/pdf, image/png, application/msword etc. purely by filename.
content_type_derivation.is_it_a_defect: NO, as shipped — an HTML payload named .png is served as image/png WITH x-content-type-options: nosniff, content-security-policy (object-src none; form-action self; frame-ancestors self) AND content-disposition: attachment, so the browser will not sniff or execute it.
content_type_derivation.caveat_for_VCST-5996: This defence depends on the attachment disposition and nosniff. If VCST-5996 is fixed by enabling INLINE disposition for previewable types, nosniff must stay and the content type must stop being taken on trust from the filename.

filename_encoding.verdict: NO DEFECT — an earlier suspicion was RETRACTED
filename_encoding.what_happened: A curl upload of a Cyrillic filename came back as U+FFFD replacement characters, which looked like server-side corruption.
filename_encoding.how_it_was_settled: Re-sent with the multipart body constructed by hand so the filename is controlled at the protocol level rather than read off the Windows filesystem. Cyrillic, Chinese and emoji filenames then round-tripped BYTE-IDENTICAL.
filename_encoding.conclusion: The mojibake was the Git Bash / Windows locale mangling the name before curl ever sent it. Not a product defect. Likewise the trailing-dot case: sent properly it is correctly rejected with INVALID_EXTENSION; the earlier http=000 was curl unable to open a Windows file ending in a dot.
